Blood transports substances and defends the body. It contains plasma and formed elements. Plasma is about 55% of blood and carries proteins, nutrients, hormones and wastes. Red blood cells contain haemoglobin and transport oxygen. White blood cells defend the body against infection. Platelets help in blood clotting. The average adult has about 5 L of blood.

Hypertension, atherosclerosis and heart attack are common disorders.

Neurons transmit electrical impulses. The resting potential and action potential depend on ion movement across the membrane. A neuron has dendrites, a cell body and an axon. t: Magnetic Force and Motion of Charges
x: Moving charges experience magnetic forces and produce magnetic fields. The force is perpendicular to velocity and field. Force F = qvB sin θ; a charge at rest experiences no magnetic force. Torque τ = mB sin θ; potential energy U = −mB cos θ. Earth's magnetic field has components: declination, dip and horizontal component. Materials respond differently to magnetic fields: diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic. Hysteresis affects energy loss in transformers. Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by magnetic fields. Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted; alignment is lost when the field is removed. Changing magnetic flux induces an EMF. Lenz's law gives the direction of the induced current. Magnetic flux φ = BA cos θ. Faraday's law: induced EMF ε = −dφ/dt. Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change producing it. A changing field or changing area can change flux. Induced EMF appears in a conductor moving through a field: ε = Bvl.

Changing current in a coil induces EMF in the same or a nearby coil. This is inductance. Self-inductance ε = −L dI/dt; L is measured in henries (H). Energy stored in an inductor U = ½LI2. Mutual inductance M relates flux in one coil to current in another. Inductors oppose changes in current, analogue to inertia. Transformers use mutual induction to change AC voltage.

Semiconductors have conductivity between conductors and insulators, controlled by doping. Silicon and germanium are the common semiconductors. Evolution is change in populations over time. Evidence comes from fossils, comparative anatomy and molecular data. Fossils document extinct forms and transitional species. Mutation, recombination and migration generate genetic variation.

Pathogens cause disease. The immune system defends the body through innate and acquired immunity. Innate immunity is non-specific and present from birth. Drug and alcohol abuse damages health and society; awareness and support are important.

x: Microbes improve soil fertility, break down waste and control pests. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in legume roots. Mycorrhiza improves phosphorus uptake in plants. Biotechnology uses living systems to make useful products. Recombinant DNA technology joins DNA from different sources. Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences. DNA ligase joins DNA fragments. Plasmids act as vectors to carry genes into host cells. The polymerase chain reaction amplifies DNA exponentially. Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size.

Genetic engineering raises opportunities and ethical questions. Safety and regulation are essential. A clone is genetically identical to its parent organism. Bioreactors provide controlled conditions for large-scale culture. Downstream processing purifies the product. Genetic engineering requires biosafety and ethical guidelines. GM organisms must be assessed for environmental and health effects.

Biotechnology improves crops, animals and human health. GM crops have traits such as pest resistance, herbicide tolerance and improved nutrition. Bt crops carry a bacterial gene for pest resistance. Golden rice was developed to increase vitamin A content. Recombinant insulin, vaccines and gene therapy have medical applications. Molecular diagnosis detects diseases at an early stage.

Transgenic animals are used for research, medicine and food, raising ethical concerns. Transgenic animals carry foreign genes in their genome. They are used to study diseases, produce medicines and improve livestock. Cloning and transgenics require strict ethical review. Biosafety and informed consent are important principles. Benefits must be balanced against animal welfare and environmental risk

Ecosystems have producers, consumers and decomposers. Energy flows one way; nutrients cycle. Solar energy is captured by producers through photosynthesis. Nutrients cycle through biogeochemical cycles (carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus). Decomposers return nutrients to the soil.

Ecosystems change over time through succession and provide services essential for humans. Primary succession begins on bare rock; secondary succession follows disturbance.
